title: Global cyclic cohesive transaction, cutback, restart and named 3D interfaces
purpose: Verify the structure-level lifecycle and native finite-element equilibrium foundation required before a calibrated cylinder fatigue-crack benchmark: exact cycle coordinates, peak/valley equilibrium, bulk/cohesive consistent tangents, post-damage feedback, atomic rollback, restart and multiple named cohesive surfaces on one mesh.
physics: Quasi-static force-controlled fixed-path Mode-I cohesive fatigue

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_fatigue_fracture.py && mpirun -n 2 python -m pytest -q tests/test_parallel_cohesive.py
execution.evidence: Analytical material-point extrema, a controlled structural surrogate and a real force-controlled Neo-Hookean split strip exercise exact and jumped cycles, structural feedback cutback, native PETSc Newton assembly, strong-constraint reaction, field/interface/ledger restart, atomic two-surface splitting and two-rank state synchronization.

observables: Accepted and rejected cycle blocks with exact integer start/end identity.
Maximum fatigue-damage increment and normalized post-damage opening feedback.
Peak, verification-peak and closing equilibrium evidence.
Bulk field, named physical-facet state and cycle ledger after restart.
Independent lower/upper cohesive surface identity on one three-dimensional solver mesh.
acceptance: No candidate block crosses a requested landing cycle.
A feedback violation restores bulk and every named interface before halving the jump.
Interrupted in-memory and durable restart paths recover the continuous accepted state.
Disjoint named surfaces duplicate nodes atomically and ambiguous shared-node surfaces are rejected.
Two MPI ranks retain identical cycle ledgers and advance all owned cohesive quadrature states to the same accepted cycle.
The 2D/3D cohesive algorithmic tangent matches force directional derivatives and the two-rank native Newton result preserves the prescribed force/reaction balance.
A native FEM cycle interrupted after one accepted cycle restarts to the same three-cycle displacement and fatigue state as the continuous calculation.
limitations: The native strip verifies the equilibrium architecture, not a calibrated cylinder finite-element solution.
Reference-point distributing-coupling work and complete monotonic/fatigue energy closure remain required.
Bulk durable checkpoint shards currently require the same MPI partition and rank count.
No calibrated material, CT geometry or retained experimental prediction is included.
